record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Develop a general dynamical-systems theory for ell-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators. The theory should include Lyapunov functions, descriptions of limit-point sets of trajectories, and other structural results governing the asymptotic behavior of the iterates of an ell-Volterra QSO.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Develop theory of dynamical systems generated by a ℓ-Volterra QSO. Find its Lyapunov functions, the set of limit points of its trajectories etc.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m:x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ be the (m−1)-dimensional standard simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) is a mapping $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ defined by
$$(Vx)_k=\sum_{i,j=1}^m p_{ij,k}\,x_i x_j,\qquad k=1,\dots,m,$$
where the coefficients satisfy $p_{ij,k}=p_{ji,k}\ge 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m p_{ij,k}=1$ for all $i,j$.

Fix an integer $\ell\in\{0,1,\dots,m\}$ and a subset $I\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}$ with $|I|=\ell$. The QSO $V$ is called an $\ell$-Volterra operator (with respect to $I$) if
$$p_{ij,k}=0\quad\text{whenever }k\notin\{i,j\}\text{ and }\{i,j\}\cap I=\varnothing,$$
i.e., the operator behaves as a classical Volterra QSO on the indices outside $I$ while allowing arbitrary stochastic coefficients on pairs involving an index in $I$. (For $\ell=0$ one recovers the classical Volterra QSOs; for $\ell=m$ one recovers all QSOs.)

For an initial point $x^{(0)}\in S^{m-1}$, the trajectory is the sequence $x^{(n+1)}=V(x^{(n)})$, $n\ge 0$, and its $\omega$-limit set $\omega(x^{(0)})$ is the set of limit points of $\{x^{(n)}\}_{n\ge 0}$ in $S^{m-1}$.

Problem. Develop a general dynamical-systems theory for $\ell$-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators on $S^{m-1}$. In particular:
(a) Construct Lyapunov functions $\varphi:S^{m-1}\to\mathbb{R}$ (i.e., continuous functions for which $\varphi\circ V$ compares monotonically with $\varphi$) suitable for arbitrary $\ell$-Volterra QSOs.
(b) Describe the set of fixed points and periodic points of $V$.
(c) Describe the structure of $\omega(x^{(0)})$ for every $x^{(0)}\in S^{m-1}$, including conditions ensuring convergence to a fixed point, convergence to a periodic orbit, or more complicated asymptotic behavior.
(d) Establish further structural results governing the asymptotic dynamics of the iterates of an $\ell$-Volterra QSO.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears partially solved. For specific subclasses of ℓ-Volterra QSOs, Lyapunov functions have been constructed and used to obtain upper estimates of ω-limit sets, and the fixed-point sets have been characterized. However, a complete general dynamical-systems theory for arbitrary ℓ-Volterra QSOs—covering all Lyapunov functions and full descriptions of limit sets—remains open, and the broader question of asymptotic behavior of QSOs is still considered open in general.

status_evidence.title: On ℓ-Volterra Quadratic Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Under some conditions on coefficients of ℓ-Volterra operators we describe Lyapunov functions and upper estimates of the set of ω-limit points of trajectories.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results: Lyapunov functions and ω-limit estimates exist under conditions on coefficients.

status_evidence.title: Lyapunov functions and dynamics of infinite dimensional Volterra operators
status_evidence.snippet: Subclasses of infinite-dimensional Lotka–Volterra operators are introduced with Lyapunov functions constructed for each subclass.
status_evidence.claim: Active research; full theory not yet complete.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of Infinite Dimensional Lotka–Volterra Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work continues to develop dynamics for Volterra-type stochastic operators.
status_evidence.claim: Topic remains an active area with new partial results.
